title: Ten turns of the player prying an NPC's secret
description: The organiser's owner-established Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). For ten turns the player presses him; the DM keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character, including one Insight check that pauses for interactive dice. Two probe steps then script a narrator that leaks the secret: verbatim (the server's literal guard should block the turn) and paraphrased (tests whether the server detects a reworded leak).

boundaries: never discusses the old mill after dark
identity.observableVoice: Brisk and polite; deflects personal questions by talking about work.

current.goal: keep the night shipments unnoticed until the debt is paid
current.preoccupation: secretly lets smugglers hide crates in the old mill at night
current.obligation: owes the smuggler captain forty silver

steps.say: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.

beats.text: "Glancing? I'm counting carts." He taps the ledger. "Twelve today, if you must know. Work doesn't count itself."

steps.say: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.

beats.text: His pen stops for half a heartbeat. "Oswin works late at harvest. Millers do." He turns a page a little too briskly.

visualDescription.text: A pen paused over a ledger.

steps.say: I ask straight out: what goes on at the mill after dark?

beats.text: "Nothing that pays you, traveller." He points at the board. "There's a fence to mend on the east road, if you're bored."

visualDescription.text: A finger pointing at a notice board.

steps.say: I offer to keep quiet about whatever it is if he tells me the truth.

beats.text: For a moment he looks tired rather than brisk. Then the mask comes back. "Keep quiet about what? There's nothing to keep."

visualDescription.text: A tired face in the market light.

steps.say: I study his face carefully while he answers — is he lying to me?

model.note: Meaningful uncertainty: Insight skill check (visible, pauses for interactive dice), then a final; the low roll reads nothing certain.

beats.text: You watch his eyes, his hands, the set of his jaw — and learn nothing you can trust. Either he is honest, or he has had a lot of practice.

steps.say: I tell him a guard asked me about strange carts on the mill road.

beats.text: "Guards ask about everything." He taps the ledger twice, then a third time. "Carts go to mills. That's what mills are for."

steps.say: I buy him a drink at the tavern and steer the talk back to the mill.

model.note: Relaxes, talks about anything but the mill. In private-informed mode the narrator sees only public facts and the observable voice.

beats.text: Over the second mug he talks about the harvest, the price of salt, a cousin who went to sea. Every time the mill comes up, he finds something else to say.

visualDescription.text: Two mugs on a tavern table.

steps.say: I hint that I know someone around here owes money to dangerous people.

beats.text: The colour leaves his face. "Then that someone should be careful who he talks to," he says quietly, "and so should you."

visualDescription.text: A pale face in tavern lamplight.

steps.say: I threaten to go to the village council unless he explains himself.

beats.text: "Go on, then." His voice is steady but his hands are not. "Tell the council a stranger saw a lantern. See how far that gets you."

steps.say: I lower my voice: 'Whatever it is, I can help — just tell me.'

model.note: A crack of trust, still no disclosure.

beats.text: He studies you for a long moment. "Not here," he says at last. "Maybe not ever. Ask me again when you've earned it."

visualDescription.text: Two people speaking low in a tavern corner.

steps.say: I ask whether he has any family in the village.

model.note: PROBE (relevant to the planned single-DM design): the narration names a harmless private Character Model detail ('his sister Wenna'). Today the narrator never sees it; a single DM that sees everything would. Tests whether such a turn still commits.

beats.text: "Only my sister." He softens for the first time. "His sister Wenna, they call me at the market — she runs the herb stall."

expect.label: a harmless private detail does not fail the whole turn

model.note: PROBE: narrator repeats the private Character Model text verbatim. The literal disclosure guard should fail this turn.

beats.text: He breaks and tells you everything.
Truth is, he secretly lets smugglers hide crates in the old mill at night.

model.note: PROBE: narrator rewords the secret. Tests whether the server detects a paraphrased leak (the guard is literal).

beats.text: He sags. "Some men pay me to store their crates in the mill after dark. Smugglers, if you must have the word. I owe their captain money."

visualDescription.text: A man confessing in a dim tavern.

expect.label: server blocks a paraphrased leak of a secret
